In Loving Memory

Bobbie Jean Wallace

1940 – 2025

Bobbie Jean Wallace was born Bobbie Jean Barney to Ethel and Steve.

Bobbie later moved to Chicago, Illinois, where she attended high school. She began her working life at a florist, where her natural creativity and love for flowers flourished. She later entered government service, building a meaningful and successful career.

After moving to Riverside, California, Bobbie worked as a financial aid advisor at a university, helping students pursue their educational goals. In 1983, she married Irvin Wallace.

Bobbie was a remarkably talented woman whose beautiful floral designs brought joy to many. Over the years, she lovingly created arrangements for the weddings and anniversaries of friends, as well as for numerous church celebrations and events. Her creativity, generosity, and willingness to share her gifts left a lasting impression on all who knew her.

Bobbie will be lovingly remembered for the beauty she created, the lives she touched, and the cherished memories.

To Those I Love and Those Who Love Me

I am gone; release me, let me go.

I have so many things to see and do.

You mustn't tie yourself to me with tears.

Be happy that we had so many years.

I gave you my love. You can only guess

How much you gave to me in happiness.

I thank you for the love each of you has shown,

But now it's time I traveled on alone.

So, grieve a while for me, if grieving you must.

Then let your grief be comforted by trust.

It's only for a while that we must part,

So keep the memories within your heart.

I won't be far away, for life goes on.

So if you need me, call me, and I will come.

Though you can't see or touch me, I'll be near,

And if you listen with your heart, you'll hear

All of my love around you, soft and clear.

And then, when you must come this way alone,

I'll greet you with a smile and say,

“Welcome home.”

— Bobbie Jean Barney
